Security Profile for InfoSec

Threat model, network perimeter, hardening, audit, and recommendations

Security Profile

Security Model Overview

The platform uses a multi-layered security model: TLS termination at the reverse proxy, JWT-based authentication with refresh token rotation, role-based access control (RBAC), container isolation with resource limits, and structured logging with centralized aggregation.

AreaStatusKey Mechanisms
AuthenticationImplementedArgon2id, JWT (15 min), refresh rotation, HttpOnly cookies
AuthorizationImplementedRBAC, permission merge (OR / MAX / UNION)
TransportImplementedTLS 1.2/1.3, HSTS preload, security headers
AuditPartialstructlog + Loki, no dedicated security trail
Rate limitingNot implementedOnly email resend (60s cooldown)
Container hardeningPartialResource limits, healthchecks, but root user

Network Perimeter and TLS

TLS is terminated at the reverse proxy (Nginx). All HTTP requests are forcibly redirected to HTTPS. TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 protocols with AEAD ciphers are supported.

Security headers

HeaderValuePurpose
Strict-Transport-Securitymax-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preloadEnforced HTTPS for 2 years
X-Content-Type-OptionsnosniffPrevents MIME-sniffing
X-Frame-OptionsSAMEORIGINClickjacking protection

Service Exposure

ServiceExternal AccessNotes
Reverse proxyYes (443/tcp)Single entry point for users
API serviceVia proxyNot directly accessible in production
DatabaseHost onlyPort forwarded to host, not externally
CacheHost onlySame as database
Object storageHost onlyManagement console on a separate port
MonitoringHost onlyDashboards, metrics, logs
Missing Content-Security-Policy The CSP header is not configured. It is recommended to add a basic policy to protect against XSS injection via inline scripts.
No rate limiting at the reverse proxy level The limit_req / limit_conn directives are not configured. All requests are proxied to the API without frequency restrictions.

Authentication Hardening

MechanismImplementationDetails
Password hashingArgon2idargon2-cffi library, modern memory-hard algorithm
JWT access tokenHS256, 15 minShort TTL minimizes the window in case of compromise
JWT refresh token7 daysStored in DB as SHA-256 hash, rotated on use
CookiesHttpOnly, SameSite=LaxSecure flag is automatically enabled over HTTPS
OAuthGoogle, GitHubstate validation via cookie, automatic email_verified
Email verificationDedicated JWT24-hour TTL, single-use by purpose purpose: email_verify
Domain policyWhitelistConfigurable allowed_email_domain + guest list
No brute force protection The authentication endpoint has no rate limiting or account lockout. With a sufficient number of attempts, password brute-forcing is possible. Recommendation: implement progressive delay or IP-based throttling.
No CSRF tokens Cookie-based sessions use SameSite=Lax, which partially protects against CSRF. However, classic CSRF tokens are not implemented for state-changing POST requests from third-party contexts.

Data Protection

In transit

All traffic between client and server is protected by TLS. Internal traffic between containers travels over the Docker network without encryption (typical model for single-host deployment).

Secrets and keys

TypeProtection
API keys (ipx_)SHA-256 hash in DB, original is not stored. Instant revocation via is_active
Refresh tokensSHA-256 hash in DB, rotated on each use
PasswordsArgon2id, irreversible hashing
Configuration secretsEnvironment variables file on the server, not in the repository
No encryption at rest The database and object storage do not use application-level encryption. It is recommended to enable disk encryption (dm-crypt/LUKS) or use managed services with built-in encryption.
No backup encryption policy The backup creation and encryption procedure is not formalized in the configuration.

Container Security

Implemented

MeasureDetails
Base imagepython:3.11-slim — minimal package set
Resource limitsCPU and memory are limited for each service (API, worker, DB, cache, etc.)
Health checksConfigured for API, DB, cache, and object storage
Log rotationjson-file driver, limit 10 MB / 3 files per container
Containers run as root The Dockerfile lacks a USER directive. All processes inside containers run with root privileges. Recommendation: add a non-root user and security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true].
No read-only root filesystem Containers can write to their filesystem. Recommendation: add read_only: true with explicit tmpfs mounts for temporary files.
Capabilities not dropped cap_drop: [ALL] is not configured, and only necessary capabilities are not explicitly added. Extended attack surface in case of container compromise.

Audit and Logging

ComponentImplementation
Log formatStructured JSON via structlog
Request contextrequest_id, tenant_id, tenant_name via contextvars
Access logMethod, path, query, status, duration, IP, User-Agent, sizes
TracingResponse header X-Request-ID for correlation
AggregationCentralized log aggregation with 30-day retention
MCP auditmcp_request_log table: tool, key, timestamp, parameters
Classification5xx → error, 4xx/slow → warning, rest → info
File logs The application writes three files: main log, error log, and access log. Each with rotation and archive count limits.
No dedicated security audit trail Failed login attempts, access denials, and role changes are not separated into a dedicated security stream. For SIEM integration, it is recommended to create a separate security logger with events: auth_failed, permission_denied, token_revoked, role_changed.

Risk Matrix and Recommendations

Summary of identified risks prioritized by severity with remediation recommendations.

RiskSeverityCurrent StatusRecommendation
Brute force on authentication endpointHIGHNot protectedRate limiting at the application or reverse proxy level
Missing Content-Security-PolicyMEDIUMNo headerAdd CSP to the reverse proxy configuration
Root processes in containersMEDIUMAll containersAdd non-root user to Dockerfile, cap_drop: [ALL]
No encryption at restMEDIUMDB and storagedm-crypt/LUKS at disk level or managed encryption
No security audit trailMEDIUMAccess log onlySeparate security events into a dedicated stream / SIEM
Service ports forwarded to hostLOWDev configurationRemove DB and cache port forwarding in production compose
Error tracking not activatedLOWPackage connectedActivate initialization when DSN is available
